This small plot near my home is where I keep my coffee and a few fruit trees — it is precious to me because it brings cash and food for my family. I cannot afford much chemical fertilizer, but I always carry manure from our animals to spread around the trees, and my husband and I do most of the work ourselves. The rains in Oromia are usually enough for the trees, so I do not irrigate, and I only use the seedlings I raised myself or got from neighbors. If the coffee berry disease comes badly I may buy a little chemical to spray, but mostly I rely on weeding and pruning by hand.
